Q: How can I split comma separated strings and remove duplicates? A:

Use the following

=INDEX(UNIQUE(TRIM(FLATTEN(SPLIT(FILTER(B3:B9, B3:B9<>""),",")))))

If your other tab is Sheet1 then use Sheet1!B3:B9

(Do adjust the formula according to your ranges and locale)

Q: Move player using keyboard in javascript A:

let player = {
x: 100,
y: 100,
speed: 5
};

const playerElement = document.getElementById('playerElement');

document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
switch(e.key) {
case 'ArrowUp':
player.y -= player.speed;
break;
case 'ArrowDown':
player.y += player.speed;
break;
case 'ArrowLeft':
player.x -= player.speed;
break;
case 'ArrowRight':
player.x += player.speed;
break;
}

// Update the HTML element's position on the screen
playerElement.style.left = player.x + 'px';
playerElement.style.top = player.y + 'px';

console.log(`Player position: x=${player.x}, y=${player.y}`);
});

Q: How much stack space is allocated for char buffer[500] variable? A:

No. You define the array as having 500 elements. If you go outside of that you will have undefined behavior. Exactly what happens depends on what the compiler are using that extra space for. Anyway, it's not yours to use.

Q: When generating code for arm64, why do gcc + clang use adrp+add rather than adr for addressing nearby variables? A:

What's being missed here is that the compiler does not know that the label is within 1MiB. It may look like the string immediately follows the branch, but that's because you have Godbolt set to filter out assembler directives, and it has filtered out a directive that switches to a different section.

Without the filtering we have

 .text            // <---------------------
.Ltext0:
  .align 2
  .global xyz()
  .type xyz(), %function
xyz():
.LFB0:
  .file 1 "/app/example.cpp"
  .loc 1 4 1 view -0
  .cfi_startproc
  .loc 1 5 2 view .LVU1
  .loc 1 5 7 is_stmt 0 view .LVU2
  mov w2, 4
  adrp x1, .LC0
  mov w0, 2
  add x1, x1, :lo12:.LC0
  b write(int, void const*, int)
.LVL0:
  .cfi_endproc
.LFE0:
  .size xyz(), .-xyz()
  .section .rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1  // <------------
.LC0:
  .string "abc"

So the adr instruction is in section .text, but the string is in section .rodata.str1.1, a subsection of the .rodata read-only data section. If this code is part of a much larger program, it is very possible that when the program is linked, those sections end up more than 1 MiB apart. The compiler has no way to know how much more of the program exists beyond this translation unit.

As Florian points out, you can force that assumption with -mcmodel=tiny, but if your program should end up being larger than 1 MiB of code plus static data, it will fail to link.

Q: Jekyll compiling seems WAY too slow A:

You could render only the latest post:

jekyll serve --watch --limit_posts 1

It is almost twice as fast in my case. Even better, rebuild only what changed:

jekyll serve --incremental

Up to 30 times faster in my case! Unfortunately only works for blog posts and some pages.
